caption: Comment "LLM" and i'll send you the repo + my setup guide 👇  the best open models have been paywalled by hardware, not price.  llama 3.3 70B is free to download. running it costs 140GB of VRAM, which means students and researchers rent thousand-dollar compute nodes to touch a model that costs nothing.  airllm breaks that math. its an open-source python library (22.4k stars) that runs 70B models on a single 4GB gpu, or a macbook.  how: inference executes a model layer by layer, in order, ~80 layers for a 70B llama. no rule says they all have to sit in memory at once. airllm loads one layer, runs it, dumps it, loads the next. peak VRAM is one layer, about 1.6GB.  nothing is quantized by default, so the output is bit-identical to running the same weights on an A100 node.  the tradeoff: time. every token reads the full model off disk, so expect seconds per token even on fast NVMe. fine for offline jobs and testing 70B output before renting real hardware. not fine for chat.  setup is pip install airllm plus one script. i wrote the whole thing up, disk requirements and all.  comment "llm" and i'll send you the repo + setup guide 👇  #airllm #llama3 #localllm #opensource #selfhosting aiengineering machinelearning

creator: psx_archive
caption: The Unholy War may be one of the PlayStation's most overlooked masterpieces. Developed by Toys for Bob, it traces its lineage back to Archon (1983), the legendary Atari 8-bit strategy game that blended chess-like tactics with arcade combat. Those ideas evolved through Star Control before finally arriving on PlayStation in glorious 3D.  This reel showcases the arena combat portion of the game. When opposing forces met on the battlefield, players took direct control of their units in fast-paced one-on-one battles. Every creature featured its own attacks, movement abilities, and strategy, making each encounter feel completely different.  Perhaps most fascinating is what happened next. Rather than receiving a simple Japanese translation, The Unholy War was completely reimagined as Majokko Daisakusen: Little Witching Mischiefs (魔女っ子大作戦). Developed by Toys for Bob in collaboration with Bandai, virtually everything was replaced—the characters, artwork, music, story, and presentation—all featuring classic magical girl anime heroines from Japan while preserving the brilliant gameplay underneath. It's one of the very few PlayStation games to receive such an extensive territorial makeover.  From Archon to Star Control, The Unholy War, and Little Witching Mischiefs, this forgotten PlayStation gem has quite the family tree.  Did you know these two games shared the same DNA? creator: thephysicist_boy
caption: Markov Chain ✍️  It explains how systems can evolve step by step, where the next move depends only on the present state and not on the full history. Imagine walking through a maze, flipping between weather conditions, or moving from one webpage to another. At every step, your next destination is chosen by a set of probabilities linked only to where you are right now.  A Markov chain treats each possible situation as a “state” and connects them with chances of moving from one state to another. If you are in a sunny state, there may be a high chance of staying sunny and a smaller chance of turning rainy. Once the next step is chosen, the past no longer matters — the system “forgets” everything except its current position.  Over many steps, patterns begin to emerge. Some states may appear more often, some may rarely be visited, and in many systems the probabilities settle into a stable long-term balance called the steady-state distribution. This reveals the hidden rhythm beneath seemingly random motion.  Scientists use Markov chains to model weather, genetics, stock markets, search engines, and even language generation. By following these probabilistic transitions, they can predict behavior, analyze uncertainty, and understand how complex systems move through time.#physics #science #fyp #amazing #explore

caption: Comment "vision" and I'll send you the demo + setup links 👇  qwen3-vl just got killed by nvidia. one 3b model. 10x faster on bounding-box detection.  every existing vision-language model predicts boxes the same way it predicts text. one corner at a time. x1, then y1, then x2, then y2. four sequential predictions per box. on a dense scene with 200 boxes that's 800 steps.  nvidia's trick: parallel box decoding. predict the entire coordinate set in a single step.  🎯 12.7 boxes/sec on h100. qwen3-vl runs at 1.1. that's the 10x.  📦 one model, four jobs: object detection, gui grounding, ocr, document layout.  🧠 trained on 138m language queries across 12m images. 785m bounding boxes.  🏆 screenspot-pro sota at 60.3 f1. that's the gui-grounding benchmark every computer-use agent is bottlenecked on.  🔓 fully open. weights on hugging face, code on github, live demo in browser. no api, no waitlist.  the catch: it's a grounding specialist, not a general vlm. it finds the thing, it doesn't reason about it. pair it with a planner llm for the full agent loop.  if you're building anything that clicks buttons, scrapes screens, or parses docs, this is the unlock.  comment "vision" for the demo + repo + the full breakdown on my site 👇  #nvidia #computervision #aiagents #opensource #huggingface
